assessments.title: Engineering needs and stakeholders: Tutorial W1-day-0 S1
assessments.description: Tutorial assessment for week 1, day 0, slot 1: apply engineering needs and stakeholders to this case: A low-cost hand-powered water carrier for a rural clinic must be usable by staff with different strengths. Focus: Translate stakeholder needs into functions before selecting a mechanism. Use evidence, units, and explicit assumptions.
learning_objectives: Translate an engineering need into a measurable requirement and identify its verification evidence.
Apply a relevant model or calculation with consistent SI units and state its assumptions.
Compare design choices using safety, performance, manufacturing, maintenance, and lifecycle constraints.

questions.prompt: A low-cost hand-powered water carrier for a rural clinic must be usable by staff with different strengths. Project note: operators report inconsistent output during cold starts. Which principle should guide the first defensible decision in engineering needs and stakeholders?
options: material behavior depends on load, environment, geometry, and time
Translate stakeholder needs into functions before selecting a mechanism.
requirements should be measurable and verified under stated conditions
a force balance must include every external load and reaction
questions.correct_answer: Translate stakeholder needs into functions before selecting a mechanism.
questions.rationale: Translate stakeholder needs into functions before selecting a mechanism.. This addresses the governing behavior in engineering needs and stakeholders before detailed design.

questions.prompt: For a preliminary check of a low-cost hand-powered water carrier for a rural clinic must be usable by staff with different strengths under conditions where operators report inconsistent output during cold starts, a load-bearing component carries 10 kN axially over 300 mm^2. What is its average normal stress?
options: 16.7 MPa, from an incorrect force-area conversion.
103 MPa, from an incorrect force-area conversion.
33.3333 MPa, because 10 kN divided by 300 mm^2 equals 33.3333 N/mm^2.
66.7 MPa, from an incorrect force-area conversion.
questions.correct_answer: 33.3333 MPa, because 10 kN divided by 300 mm^2 equals 33.3333 N/mm^2.
questions.rationale: Convert 10 kN to 10000 N and divide by 300 mm^2. One N/mm^2 equals one MPa, giving 33.3333 MPa; local concentrations are excluded.

questions.prompt: Given that operators report inconsistent output during cold starts, how should the team express a requirement for the engineering needs and stakeholders application?
options: Say the design should be robust and leave performance to the supplier.
Name a preferred component and treat that choice as proof of need.
Set a target after testing so the observed result automatically passes.
State an observable threshold, its operating conditions, and a specified verification method.
questions.correct_answer: State an observable threshold, its operating conditions, and a specified verification method.
questions.rationale: A threshold, conditions, and method make a need testable without prematurely selecting a solution.

questions.prompt: Before modeling a low-cost hand-powered water carrier for a rural clinic must be usable by staff with different strengths while operators report inconsistent output during cold starts, what should the analysis record?
options: The system boundary, inputs, outputs, interfaces, and assumptions that affect the decision.
Every nearby object whether or not it exchanges force, energy, or information.
No assumptions, because ideal behavior is universally valid.
Only the model that gives the preferred result.
questions.correct_answer: The system boundary, inputs, outputs, interfaces, and assumptions that affect the decision.
questions.rationale: A boundary and explicit assumptions clarify what is included and where the model may not apply.

questions.prompt: A component associated with engineering needs and stakeholders fails earlier than predicted while operators report inconsistent output during cold starts. What is the strongest initial diagnosis?
options: Repeat the same test and infer cause only from whether it fails again.
Preserve evidence and inspect load path, geometry, boundary conditions, and service environment.
Increase nominal strength immediately without preserving the failed part or history.
Assume the material batch is defective because a calculation was once checked.
questions.correct_answer: Preserve evidence and inspect load path, geometry, boundary conditions, and service environment.
questions.rationale: Failure analysis tests plausible mechanisms and assumptions before prescribing a corrective action.

questions.prompt: During work on a low-cost hand-powered water carrier for a rural clinic must be usable by staff with different strengths, where operators report inconsistent output during cold starts, an exposed energy source could injure a technician. What control is strongest?
options: Use personal protective equipment as the only measure even when guarding is feasible.
Ask workers to be careful and count the instruction as risk reduction.
Eliminate or isolate the hazard where feasible, then use and verify an engineered safeguard.
Rely on a warning while leaving access and energy unchanged.
questions.correct_answer: Eliminate or isolate the hazard where feasible, then use and verify an engineered safeguard.
questions.rationale: Elimination and engineered isolation reduce exposure at its source and are more reliable than warnings alone.

questions.prompt: If conditions change in the engineering needs and stakeholders system because operators report inconsistent output during cold starts, which strategy can correct a measured deviation?
options: Keep a fixed actuator command regardless of measured output.
Increase controller gain without checking delay, saturation, or stability.
Remove the sensor so disturbances cannot affect the command.
Use feedback with a suitable sensor, defined setpoint, actuator limits, and tested safe response.
questions.correct_answer: Use feedback with a suitable sensor, defined setpoint, actuator limits, and tested safe response.
questions.rationale: Feedback acts on measured error, while sensor quality, actuator limits, and stability bound its safe use.

questions.prompt: Given that operators report inconsistent output during cold starts, how should the team select a process for manufacturing a part used in engineering needs and stakeholders?
options: Check geometry, material, tolerance, finish, production volume, cost, and inspection capability together.
Choose the lowest unit-price process while ignoring setup, scrap, and tolerance.
Use additive manufacturing for every shape because complexity guarantees strength.
Specify the tightest tolerance on every surface regardless of function.
questions.correct_answer: Check geometry, material, tolerance, finish, production volume, cost, and inspection capability together.
questions.rationale: Process selection is constrained by capability, geometry, material, volume, finish, cost, and inspection.

questions.prompt: How should the team verify a revised design for engineering needs and stakeholders when operators report inconsistent output during cold starts?
options: Measure a convenient proxy unrelated to the stated requirement.
Link each requirement to representative conditions, capable instruments, and predeclared acceptance limits.
Show one successful run and infer performance under all conditions.
Set acceptance limits after seeing results so ordinary variation passes.
questions.correct_answer: Link each requirement to representative conditions, capable instruments, and predeclared acceptance limits.
questions.rationale: Traceable tests use relevant conditions, adequate measurement, and criteria fixed before results.

questions.prompt: Two concepts meet the immediate engineering needs and stakeholders target, but operators report inconsistent output during cold starts. How should the decision be justified?
options: Hide all measurements inside an unexplained composite score.
Choose the first concept built and treat sunk effort as proof of superiority.
Compare feasible options across performance, safety, cost, maintenance, and lifecycle impacts; record sensitivity.
Select the lightest option because one metric always dominates engineering.
questions.correct_answer: Compare feasible options across performance, safety, cost, maintenance, and lifecycle impacts; record sensitivity.
questions.rationale: Explicit multi-criteria comparison exposes tradeoffs and sensitivity while retaining an auditable rationale.

assessments.concept_explanation: Engineering needs and stakeholders connects intended function to the behavior that limits performance. In this case, Translate stakeholder needs into functions before selecting a mechanism. The claim must be interpreted in context: A low-cost hand-powered water carrier for a rural clinic must be usable by staff with different strengths. A simplified model supports comparison, but its assumptions must be revisited if measurement or service evidence disagrees.
assessments.terminology_and_components: For engineering needs and stakeholders, a requirement is a testable statement of need; a constraint is a limit; an interface is a defined exchange; and verification is evidence that a requirement is met. Identify the system boundary, inputs, outputs, users, materials, and maintenance access before assigning component roles.
assessments.why_it_matters: Weak treatment of engineering needs and stakeholders can produce a concept that fails in service, costs more to maintain, or transfers risk to users. A low-cost hand-powered water carrier for a rural clinic must be usable by staff with different strengths. Decisions need traceable evidence, and clear assumptions help disciplines coordinate without silently using incompatible operating conditions.
assessments.how_it_works: Document the need and operating envelope, identify constraints and interfaces, then apply the governing idea that Translate stakeholder needs into functions before selecting a mechanism. Estimate performance with a transparent model and explicit assumptions; check critical predictions with calculations or measurements. Compare feasible options and verify the selection against criteria set before testing.
assessments.worked_examples: For A low-cost hand-powered water carrier for a rural clinic must be usable by staff with different strengths. define a performance quantity with units, draw a system boundary, and list inputs, outputs, and constraints. Make a first estimate using a transparent model, then measure a prototype in representative conditions. If estimate and observation disagree, inspect assumptions, interfaces, and instrument uncertainty before changing the design.
assessments.common_mistakes: Common errors in engineering needs and stakeholders include treating a preferred component as a requirement, assuming one nominal calculation proves safe operation, omitting boundary conditions, mixing units, ignoring tolerances or environment, and reporting tests without uncertainty or predeclared limits. Check evidence and load paths before correcting symptoms.
assessments.practical_application: For the stated case, A low-cost hand-powered water carrier for a rural clinic must be usable by staff with different strengths. Create requirements with thresholds, conditions, and verification methods. Identify a credible failure mode, select a suitable safeguard, and plan a repeatable test or inspection. Record configuration and assumptions so maintainers can use the design safely.
assessments.decisions_and_tradeoffs: Choices in engineering needs and stakeholders rarely optimize every objective. Check hard constraints first, then compare performance, cost, mass, durability, repairability, user needs, and environmental impact. State the evidence and weighting behind a preference, test sensitivity to assumptions, and keep a feasible fallback when supply or maintenance is uncertain.
